faq.q: Do I need a license to charter a yacht in Marbella in 2043?
faq.a: If you charter with a skipper (as all our boats are), you do not need a license. The skipper holds the necessary qualifications. For self-drive or bareboat charters, you would need a valid recreational craft license, but we do not offer bareboat rentals.

faq.q: What license is required for self-drive boat rental in Marbella?
faq.a: For self-drive, the Spanish 'Licencia de Navegación' (for boats up to 6m and up to 40kW) or a 'Patrón de Navegación Básica' (for up to 8m) is required. For larger vessels, a 'Patrón de Yate' or an International Certificate of Competence (ICC) may be accepted. Always check with the charter company.

faq.q: Can I use my foreign boating license in Spain?
faq.a: Yes, if it's an ICC (International Certificate of Competence) or a national license recognized by Spain. Non-EU licenses may require an official translation or an ICC. For skippered charters, your license is irrelevant as the skipper is responsible.

faq.q: What is the minimum age to charter a boat in Marbella?
faq.a: For skippered charters, there is no minimum age for passengers, but children must be accounted for in the passenger capacity. For self-drive, the minimum age varies by license type, typically 16-18 years. Our boats are all skippered, so families are welcome.

faq.q: Are there any license requirements for jet skis included in charters?
faq.a: On our Mangusta 80 charters (including the grey variant), a jet ski is included free. To drive the jet ski, you need a valid jet ski license (Spanish 'Licencia de Navegación de Motos Náuticas') or an equivalent. The skipper can provide guidance, but you must have the license to operate it.

faq.q: Do I need to show any documents when booking a skippered charter?
faq.a: For skippered charters, we only require a valid ID (passport or national ID) for each passenger for the manifest. No boating license is needed. We handle all legal requirements, including insurance and safety checks.

faq.q: What happens if I don't have a license but want to drive the boat?
faq.a: On our skippered charters, the skipper is in charge. You cannot legally take the helm without a license. However, the skipper may allow you to steer under their direct supervision, but this is at their discretion and not guaranteed.

faq.q: How do I get a Spanish boating license before my trip?
faq.a: You can obtain a Spanish recreational license through accredited schools in Spain, which typically require a theory and practical exam. For visitors, an ICC from your home country is often easier. For skippered charters, you don't need one at all.

data.body_html:
Planning a yacht charter in Marbella for 2043? The good news: if you book with a skipper (as all our boats are), you don't need a boating license. But if you're considering a self-drive option, there are specific requirements you must meet. This guide covers everything you need to know about marbella yacht charter license requirements 2043, so you can sail from Puerto Banús with confidence.

Do You Need a License for a Skippered Charter?

No. When you charter any of our boats — from the Astondoa 40 to the Ferretti 94 — a licensed skipper is included in the price. The skipper holds the required Spanish qualifications, and you simply relax and enjoy the coast. This is the simplest way to experience yachting without any paperwork.

When Is a License Required?

A license is only required if you plan to rent a boat without a skipper (bareboat). In Spain, the type of license depends on the boat's length and engine power. For example, a 'Licencia de Navegación' allows you to operate boats up to 6 metres with engines up to 40kW. For larger vessels, you need a 'Patrón de Navegación Básica' or higher. Since we only offer skippered charters, you never need to worry about this.

Spanish License Types Explained

  • Licencia de Navegación – For boats up to 6m, engine up to 40kW. Minimum age 16.
  • Patrón de Navegación Básica – For boats up to 8m, engine up to 40kW. Minimum age 18.
  • Patrón de Yate – For boats up to 24m. Requires more advanced training.
  • International Certificate of Competence (ICC) – Accepted for non-Spanish residents, often easier to obtain.

If you hold a valid ICC from your home country, it is generally recognised in Spanish waters. Always carry your original license and a passport when on board.

Our Fleet: All Skippered, No License Needed

Every boat in our fleet departs from Puerto Banús with a professional skipper. Whether you choose the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 guests) or the Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 guests), the skipper handles navigation, docking, and safety. You can even ask the skipper to teach you the ropes along the way — but legally, you're not required to hold a license.

Jet Ski Licenses on Mangusta 80 Charters

On our Mangusta 80 (Grey) and standard Mangusta 80, a jet ski is included free with a minimum 4-hour charter (€4,719). To drive the jet ski, you must hold a valid jet ski license (Spanish 'Licencia de Navegación de Motos Náuticas') or an equivalent. The skipper can provide a safety briefing, but cannot lend a license. If you don't have one, you can still enjoy the yacht and let a licensed companion drive the jet ski.

What Documents to Bring for a Skippered Charter

For any of our skippered charters, you only need a valid ID (passport or national ID card) for each passenger. We handle the rest — insurance, safety equipment, and the skipper's credentials. No boating license, no endless paperwork. Just show up at Puerto Banús and set sail towards Cabopino, Estepona, or even Sotogrande.

Legal Requirements for the Skipper

Our skippers are fully licensed under Spanish maritime law. They hold the appropriate qualifications for the vessel's size, and they're experienced with local waters — from the Golden Mile to Cala del Faro. You can trust that all safety protocols are followed, including life jackets, radio checks, and weather assessments.

How to Book with Confidence

If you have any questions about license requirements or which boat suits your group, simply contact us via WhatsApp. We'll confirm your booking, answer any queries, and ensure your charter is legal and stress-free. For a quick overview of our fleet, check our fleet page — but remember, all boats come with a skipper, so no license is needed.
